Encoded file: H.264 High, 1080x1920, yuv420p, 30/1 fps, 537 frames, duration 17.900 s (checked with ffprobe), no audio. window.STORY_DURATION = 17.9. "Still" below means the text block is fully visible and not moving. Required time = words/3 + 0.8 s.

S1 HOOK, 0.00 to 3.25
- 0.00 (thumbnail): navy scene with the full KRS logo (top centre), widened viewfinder brackets, ruler ticks, a dim waveform, and ghost-outline "WE'RE HIRING / VIDEO / EDITOR". The orange playhead is parked at the left.
- 0.12 to 1.02: the playhead sweeps left to right. A clip-path wipe synced to it turns the ghost text solid (kicker done about 0.35, VIDEO/EDITOR done about 0.95). An orange trail glow follows the playhead, and the waveform brightens behind it.
- 0.78 to 1.28: the brackets lock onto the headline with an overshoot.
- Still 1.02 to 3.25 = 2.23 s (needs 2.13 s for 4 words).

T1 CAMERA TILT, 3.25 to 3.93
- The world moves up 1000 px with a scale dip to 0.955 at mid-move.
- Vertical motion blur (SMIL feGaussianBlur, peak 20 px).
- The HUD brackets reframe with a breathe-out, and the background streaks move a little slower than the world (parallax).

S2 RULES, 3.93 to 7.45
- 3.80 to 4.38: three plain blue clips are drawn onto the tracks.
- 4.22 to 5.22: the playhead sweeps across. Behind it, clips 1 and 2 become disabled (hatching, orange border, X badges pop at 4.38 and 4.53): "NO MOBILE EDITORS" and "NO CAPCUT EDITORS". The track-3 clip renders as enabled: "✓ Professional desktop editors only".
- Still: NO MOBILE about 4.75 to 7.45 = 2.7 s (needs 1.8 s); NO CAPCUT and the check line about 5.1 to 7.45 = 2.35 s (needs 1.8 s and 2.13 s).

T2 CAMERA TILT, 7.45 to 8.13
- Same move as T1.

S3 BENEFITS, 8.13 to 13.95
- 8.07 to 8.62: the BENEFITS header builds in (slash slices in, word wipes on, rule draws).
- Clips slide in from the right and snap onto the tracks at the parked in-point playhead, with an overshoot. Each track-header number lights up and the lane outline glows once.
  - 01: 8.29 to 8.81
  - 02: 8.63 to 9.15
  - 03: 8.97 to 9.49
- Still:
  - Row 01: 8.81 to 13.95 = 5.1 s (needs 2.47 s)
  - Row 02: 9.15 to 13.95 = 4.8 s (needs 4.47 s, or 4.8 s if "&" counts as a word)
  - Row 03: 9.49 to 13.95 = 4.46 s (needs 2.8 s)

T3 BRAND SLASH WIPE, 13.95 to 14.75
- An orange band at the angle of the logo's R-leg (skew 41.5 deg) crosses the frame. A diagonal clip-path edge locked to the band reveals the end card.

S4 END CARD, 14.75 to 17.90
- 14.37 to 14.81: brackets settle.
- 14.31 to 14.87: a light glint travels along the logo's orange slash.
- 14.39 to 14.84: the APPLY NOW arrow nudges once.
- Pixel-identical from 14.84 to 17.89, so the final 3.05 s is fully still: logo, WE'RE HIRING, VIDEO / EDITOR, and the split bar "APPLY NOW →" / "DM us your portfolio".
- The CTA (6 words, needs 2.8 s) is fully visible from about 14.6, so readable for about 3.3 s.
build:cinematic.known_weaknesses:
1. Grain was removed. The poster's film-grain overlay made each frame about 1.7 MB as PNG, and the 72-frame contact sheet then crashed capture.js's setContent (about 163 MB of base64; even 5% grain was still too large). The video therefore has a clean gradient background without grain. H.264 at crf 17 shows no obvious banding in the frames I checked, but it was not checked on a phone.
2. The hold scenes are deliberately static. S2 holds about 2.4 s and S3 holds 4.5 to 5 s with only decoration settling, to meet the readability rule. Anyone tapping fast may find S3 long; S3 is still dense (about 23 words) and is the tightest on reading time.
3. Repeated device. The playhead "render" wipe is used twice (S1, S2), and S1 and the end card share the same headline layout as a deliberate bookend. Viewers may notice the repetition.
4. Fast motion:
   - The slash wipe travels about 3,000 px in 0.8 s, so frame-to-frame jumps in the middle of the wipe are large (it is a solid graphic, but it may look slightly steppy at 30 fps).
   - The camera tilts look like whip-pans, and the frame between sections is mostly blur and empty navy for about 3 frames.
5. Small-text and layout trade-offs:
   - "DM us your portfolio" is 37 px (above the 34 px minimum) and fits tightly in the right half of the CTA. The CTA is smaller than in the poster relative to the headline.
   - "PREMIUM STOCK & MOCKUP SUBSCRIPTION" wraps onto 2 lines.
   - The S3 numerals 01/02/03 sit in a left track-header column instead of on the right as in the poster.
6. Decoration bleeds outside the safe area: the brackets (x 40 to 1040, and wider while expanded), the playhead heads parked at x about 1012 (the head overlaps the top-right bracket corner in S1 and S2), the background streaks and the slash band all extend past x 64 to 1016 or y 250 to 1580. No text, logo or CTA does.
7. Copy and logo: wording is canonical, with no added facts. The two official logo paths were split into their existing subpaths (KRS / TECH / tagline / R-leg / SOLUTIONS) for animation; the geometry is unchanged and only uniform scaling is used. The logo stays the same size in the top HUD throughout and is not animated in S1. The orange R-leg is present from frame 0 so the thumbnail shows the complete logo; the brand slash is used for the end-card wipe and the glint instead.
8. The ghost-outline headline at frame 0 is fairly faint (34% white and 55% orange strokes). It reads on a phone thumbnail, but less boldly than solid text would.
9. Generator and helper scripts are in the scratchpad, not the project: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-kawin/d3ae9d3f-46af-5de8-9d5c-3a9c83446a9f/scratchpad/gen.js (all timings are in its T object), plus check.js and grid.js. The published HTML is self-contained apart from ../../assets/fonts.css.

build:kinetic.scene_timing:
The page sets window.STORY_DURATION = 17.5. ffprobe on the MP4: h264 High, 1080x1920, yuv420p, 30/1 fps, 525 frames, 17.500 s, 1.85 MB, no audio.

The rule used throughout is "still time needed = words/3 + 0.8 s". Every "still" window below was checked with pixel diffs at 0.1 s steps.

HUD (stays on top through every scene):
- Viewfinder brackets are visible at frame 0. They snap into place 0–0.32 s, then pump outward briefly on the slams (0.44 and 0.92) and at each whip (3.0, 7.0, 13.0). They are decoration only.
- The "WE'RE HIRING" kicker is fully visible and still from frame 0 to the end.
- The logo is inlined from krs-logo-white.svg, with the orange path split into the R-leg and SOLUTIONS. It is complete at frame 0. The R-leg settles 14px along its own axis while a separate orange trail retracts into it (0–0.32), so the logo is never distorted. The logo is still from 0.32.

S1 hook, 0.00–3.00:
- VIDEO slams in 0.25–0.60: scale 2.1 to 0.95 to 1 with a blur clearing, impact at 0.44. Still 0.60–3.00 = 2.4 s (needs 1.47).
- An orange brand-angle slash bar sweeps across EDITOR 0.70–0.98 and reveals it, with a scale slam settling at 1.06. Still 1.06–3.00 = 1.94 s (needs 1.47).
- Two light streaks at the R-leg angle (from the poster) draw in 0.32–0.56.
- Below the headline sits a small decorative timeline strip with unlabeled clips. Its playhead cuts on the beats (0.44, 0.92, 1.40) and stops at 1.54.

T1 whip, 3.00–3.50:
- An orange band plus a white streak, slanted at the R-leg angle, sweeps right to left (seam 3.00–3.42). It is on screen about 3.10–3.33.
- The old scene exits left with blur (3.00–3.36). The new scene enters from the right with blur and lands at 3.50.

S2 rules, 3.50–7.00:
- Large NLE timeline with two staggered clips on two tracks. Before stamping they are normal blue clips and their text is already legible.
- Playhead lands on clip 1 (3.45–3.60). The X badge stamps down 3.56–3.80: the clip goes hatched with an orange border, "NO" turns orange, and a 6-frame decaying shake ends at 3.87. NO MOBILE EDITORS is still 3.87–7.00 = 3.13 s (needs 1.8).
- Playhead moves to clip 2 (3.95–4.10), which stamps 4.06–4.30 with the shake ending at 4.37. NO CAPCUT EDITORS is still 4.37–7.00 = 2.63 s (needs 1.8).
- Playhead parks after the clips 4.40–4.58. The waveform left of the playhead brightens as it moves.
- Check badge pops 4.42–4.70 and "Professional desktop editors only" (64px) wipes in 4.46–4.74. Still 4.74–7.00 = 2.26 s (needs 2.13).

T2 whip, 7.00–7.50 (same seam whip).

S3 benefits, 7.50–13.00:
- BENEFITS header lands 7.50; its slash icon and rule draw in 7.30–7.66. Still to 13.00 = 5.5 s (needs 1.13).
- Each row snaps in on the beat: icon tile pops with overshoot, title and subtitle slide in from +90px, the numeral rolls up, the separator draws.
  - Row 01 snaps 7.50–7.84. Still 7.84–13.00 = 5.16 s (needs 2.47).
  - Row 02 snaps 8.00–8.34. Still 8.34–13.00 = 4.66 s (needs 4.47).
  - Row 03 snaps 8.50–8.84. Still 8.84–13.00 = 4.16 s (needs 2.8).
- A light sheen crosses each icon tile at 9.50, 10.00 and 10.50 as a read-along cue. No text moves.

T3 whip, 13.00–13.50 (same seam whip).

S4 end card, 13.50–17.50:
- VIDEO / EDITOR sits in the same position as in S1 and is still from 13.50.
- The split APPLY NOW bar slides in from the left 13.50–13.86. "DM us your portfolio" fades in 13.68–13.96.
- The arrow nudges once 14.00–14.36, while a sheen crosses only the orange button 13.96–14.34.
- From 14.36 to 17.50 the frame is pixel-identical (3.14 s; the CTA needs 2.8 s). The paused last frame shows the logo, WE'RE HIRING, VIDEO EDITOR and APPLY NOW → DM us your portfolio.

Safe zone: all text, the logo and the CTA sit within x 64–1016 and y 296–1442 (allowed: x 64–1016, y 250–1580). Only brackets, streaks and the whip bands bleed outside. Smallest copy is 38px (the DM line), clip labels are 60px, benefit subtitles 42px. All copy is the canonical copy only.
build:kinetic.known_weaknesses:
1. Frame 0 (the thumbnail) shows the logo, WE'RE HIRING, the brackets and the timeline strip, but the middle of the frame is empty because VIDEO only slams in at 0.25–0.44. To get "KRS — We're hiring" readable in the thumbnail, I dropped the planned reveal animation on the kicker and on SOLUTIONS. The "logo slash-in" is therefore subtle: a 14px R-leg settle plus a retracting orange trail. An earlier version had a bigger slash-in, but frame 0 then read "KPS TECH".

2. The R-leg angle is steep, so each whip band is only on screen for about 0.2 s (around 6 frames). It reads more as a hard brand-slash wipe than a true camera whip pan, and the outgoing scene's blur/slide is mostly hidden behind the band. All three transitions use the same move, which is consistent but repetitive.

3. S3 benefits is about 4.2 s of fully static text (8.84–13.0). The readability rule requires it for row 02, but it is the least kinetic stretch; only the small tile sheens move.

4. Some readability margins are thin: the pro line has 2.26 s against 2.13 s needed, and row 02 has 4.66 s against 4.47 s.

5. The poster's film-grain overlay was dropped. It made each frame about 1.6 MB, which crashed capture.js --sheet, and it would not survive Instagram's compression anyway. The look is slightly cleaner and flatter than the poster.

6. The stamp shake is a deliberate 6-frame decaying shake, as the direction asked. A strict "no jitter" reviewer might flag it. Text only moves during the stamp, before its reading time starts.

7. The end card repeats the S1 VIDEO/EDITOR layout as a bookend and adds the CTA. It does not carry the NO-rules or benefits, so a paused last frame says who is hiring and how to apply, but not the conditions.

8. The tagline inside the logo (BUILD • INNOVATE • SCALE) is about 14px high at 320px logo width, so it will be illegible on a phone. That is part of the logo, not copy.

9. The total is 17.5 s, at the long end of 15–18 s, mainly because of the benefits hold.

10. The HTML is generated by my scratch script /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-kawin/d3ae9d3f-46af-5de8-9d5c-3a9c83446a9f/scratchpad/kin/build.py, which is not a deliverable. The HTML is self-contained but has long generated keyframe lines, so hand-tuning the timing is easier through the script.

11. The shared drafts/ folder also holds a parallel run's story-cinematic* files, which are not mine. An earlier build of story-kinetic.html had been auto-committed at 04:11 (commit eebaa16). The current version is modified and uncommitted, and I made no commits.

defects: 0.00-0.27 s: the thumbnail (frame 0) is mostly empty navy. It shows only the small WE'RE HIRING kicker, the logo, brackets and a strip of unlabeled clips near y 1330. Scaled down to 160 px it reads only as a 'KRS' card, not as a VIDEO EDITOR post.

0.267 s (f7 to f8): VIDEO goes from absent to 2.1x scale in a single frame (22% of pixels change). The blurred oversized word briefly overlaps the logo and bleeds past both frame edges for about 2 frames. It is acceptable as a slam, but it has no anticipation at all.

3.67-3.87 s and 4.17-4.37 s: the stamp shake changes direction every frame (dx -8/+8/-5/+3/-1, dy +4/-4/+3/-2, measured). That is a 15 Hz, ±8 px jitter on clip text that was already readable as a blue clip from 3.27 s, so legible text is moving.

3.17-3.27 s, 7.17-7.27 s, 13.17-13.27 s: the whip band is on screen for only about 4 frames, moving about 500 px per frame. It reads as a glitchy hard cut more than a whip. The outgoing scene's eased exit (dx -1, -4, -9, -14 over f91-f94) is almost completely hidden. The same move is used 3 times.

4.40-4.43 s (f132 to f133): the playhead jumps 392 px in one frame, then eases 116, 35, 11 px. It reads as a teleport. The earlier moves (f103 to f104, +85 px, and f118 to f119, +96 px) also start at full speed with no ease-in.

4.70-7.03 s: the pro line is still for 2.33 s against 2.13 s needed (+0.20 s). 8.33-13.03 s: row 02 is still for 4.70 s against 4.47 s (+0.23 s). 14.27-17.50 s: the CTA is still for 3.23 s against 2.80 s (+0.43 s). These are the thinnest readability margins.
8.83-13.00 s: about 4.2 s of fully static benefits, with only three small tile sheens (measured at 9.70, 10.20 and 10.70 s, not the stated 9.5/10.0/10.5). This is the flattest stretch of the video.
S1 0.0-3.0 s: the decorative timeline strip of blank blue clips is filler. The concept-A timeline only does real work in S2.
Minor: from 0.00 to 0.10 s the R-leg is offset with an orange trail. At thumbnail size it reads as a slightly smeared logo, not as an intentional slash-in.
best_ideas: The EDITOR reveal at 0.73-0.98 s: an orange bar at the R-leg angle sweeps across EDITOR and reveals it, a brand-motivated reveal.

Stamp choreography: the playhead lands on each clip, the X badge stamps down, the clip turns hatched with an orange border and NO turns orange. The clip text is already legible before the stamp. Graft it without the 15 Hz shake, using a single 2-frame squash instead.
Tight rhythm: new-scene copy is legible within about 0.3 s of each transition (S2 labels at 3.27 s, BENEFITS at 7.27 s, row 01 at 7.6 s), so there is very little dead air.

Large, poster-faithful type: the pro line is 64 px outside the timeline, benefit subtitles are 42 px, numerals sit on the right as in the poster, and WE'RE HIRING plus the logo stay in the HUD the whole time.
Benefit rows snap in on 0.5 s beats (7.50, 8.00, 8.50) with the icon tile overshooting, the numeral rolling up and the separator drawing in. A clean stagger.
The waveform left of the playhead brightens as the playhead moves.
End card pixel-identical from 14.37 s to 17.50 s, with comfortable CTA padding.

defects: 3.53-3.63 s and 7.60-7.70 s: during the camera tilt the outgoing world is hard-clipped along a horizontal line at about y 465, just under the logo. VIDEO and then EDITOR are visibly sliced mid-letter by an invisible matte for 3 to 4 frames, which gives away that this is a masked viewport, not a camera move.

3.27-4.43 s and 7.47-8.40 s: about 1.1 s and 0.9 s with no readable new copy. The tilt passes through about 5 frames of blurred, nearly empty navy (3.63-3.80 s) and lands on empty lanes or blank clips. Text appears only once the playhead or the header build reaches it, so the rhythm sags twice.
0.00 s thumbnail: the ghost WE'RE HIRING (about 34% white and 55% orange stroke) is barely legible at 160 px width. VIDEO EDITOR does read.
1.00-3.27 s and 5.23-7.47 s: the parked playhead head (x about 1011-1013) sits on top of the top-right bracket corner, which clutters the corner.

5.10-7.47 s: the pro clip is still for 2.37 s against 2.13 s needed (+0.23 s). 14.73-17.90 s: the CTA is still for 3.17 s against 2.80 s (+0.37 s). NO CAPCUT is still 5.13-7.47 s (+0.53 s). The margins are thin.

8.30-9.50 s: benefit clips slide in from off-screen right and overshoot past the right bracket (to about x 1079), so the text is in motion and outside the safe x zone while it first becomes legible. This is transient but noticeable.

Type is smaller than the poster: the DM line is 37 px and packed against the right edge of the CTA, benefit subtitles are 38 px and the pro line is 42 px inside a clip. Numerals 01/02/03 moved to the left.
The tilt blur uses SMIL <animate> on feGaussianBlur rather than CSS keyframes or Web Animations. capture.js seeks it correctly, but it is outside the stated technical contract.
The playhead render-wipe device is used twice (S1 and S2), and S1 and the end card share the same layout.
best_ideas: The ghost-outline headline at frame 0, solidified by the playhead's clip-path wipe (0.12-1.0 s). The thumbnail already says VIDEO EDITOR, and the text never moves while it becomes readable.
Playhead sweeps eased properly (measured in px per frame: 1, 5, 11, 20, 30, 44, 60, 77, 90, 92, 87, 75 ... 3, 2, 0) with a synced orange trail glow and the waveform brightening behind it.

An NLE metaphor all the way through: disabled hatched clips for NO MOBILE and NO CAPCUT, an enabled blue clip for 'Professional desktop editors only', and benefits as clips snapping onto numbered tracks at the playhead in-point.

The brand-slash end wipe at 14.07-14.60 s: an orange band at the R-leg angle (41.5°) with a diagonal clip-path edge locked to it. It is on screen for about 15 frames and reads as a deliberate brand move, followed by a glint along the logo's orange slash.
The HUD brackets lock onto the headline with an overshoot, and the background streaks move at parallax during the tilts.
Biggest end-card headline: WE'RE HIRING plus VIDEO / EDITOR plus the split APPLY NOW bar, pixel-still from 14.87 s to 17.90 s.

judge:motion.reasoning:
Cinematic wins, 41 to 39. Kinetic is close and has the better rhythm and larger type.

How I checked: I used only the rendered MP4s (frame-by-frame diffs, plus per-region still windows measured against a reference frame) and capture.js --at --safe frames. Everything I wrote is in /home/user/kawin/posters/video-editor-hiring/story/judge-motion/ (sheets k-*.png, c-*.png, cmp-*.png; logs *-motion.txt; scripts in tools/). The drafts are unmodified.

Readability rule: every text block in both builds passes words/3 + 0.8. Measured still windows:
- Kinetic: pro line 2.33 s (needs 2.13), row 02 4.70 s (needs 4.47), CTA 3.23 s (needs 2.80).
- Cinematic: pro clip 2.37 s (needs 2.13), row 02 5.10 s (needs 4.47), CTA 3.17 s (needs 2.80).
- Both end cards are pixel-still for at least 3.0 s.
- Copy is canonical in both, and no static text, logo or CTA leaves the safe zone.

Why cinematic wins:
- Better thumbnail and hook: the ghost VIDEO EDITOR is legible at frame 0, while kinetic's frame 0 is mostly empty navy.
- Transitions are motivated and properly eased: playhead sweeps measured at 0 → 92 → 0 px per frame, a clip-path reveal synced to the playhead so text never moves while being read, and a brand-slash end wipe.
- It carries the concept-A timeline through every scene, not just S2.

Kinetic is punchier and tighter: copy is legible about 0.3 s after each transition, and type is bigger and closer to the poster. But its craft has hard-edged problems:
- A 15 Hz, ±8 px stamp shake on text that is already legible.
- A 4-frame whip band, repeated identically 3 times, that reads as a glitch cut.
- A 392 px one-frame jump of the playhead.
- An empty thumbnail.

Cinematic's main faults are fixable:
- A hard matte edge slices the headline during both tilts (about 3.55 s and 7.65 s).
- About 1 s of content-free dead air after each tilt.
- Small type (DM line 37 px, subtitles 38 px).
- The playhead overlaps the top-right bracket corner.
- SMIL is used for the blur.

Recommended grafts into cinematic:
- Kinetic's stamp choreography, without the shake.
- Kinetic's 64 px pro line, right-side numerals and 42 px subtitles.
- Kinetic's beat-timed row stagger.
- Pre-populated lanes so each tilt lands on readable copy.
- A feathered world mask in place of the hard clip.

defects: 0.00-0.25: the thumbnail and the first 8 frames have an empty centre. Only the small HUD kicker (54px), the logo, the brackets and a decorative strip at y~1330-1450 are visible. At phone-thumbnail size it reads 'WE'RE HIRING / KRS' with no role shown.

0.27-0.37: VIDEO enters at 2.1x scale and heavily blurred, overflowing the frame. The first sharp read is at about 0.40 s and EDITOR at about 1.06 s, so the hook is fine, but the role is not on frame 0.

3.10-3.33, 7.10-7.33, 13.10-13.33: the same R-leg slash whip is used three times. The band is on screen for only about 6 frames and covers the KRS logo at about 3.15, 7.15 and 13.15. It is repetitive and reads as a wipe, not a camera move.

3.58-3.62: the X badge fades in as a translucent blue disc over the 'NO' of clip 1 before the hard stamp at 3.65 (and the same at about 4.08 on clip 2). This makes 2 muddy frames, plus a 3-4px decaying shake to 3.87 and 4.37.
7.22-7.55: only the BENEFITS header is on screen (about 0.33 s of near-empty frame).

8.84-13.00: 4.16 s of fully static benefits with only small tile sheens. This is the longest stretch with no new information and the most likely place for a viewer to tap through, although the row 02 reading time needs most of it (4.66 vs 4.47 s).
The 'Professional desktop editors only' margin is thin: 2.26 s still against the 2.13 s needed.
Logo right edge measured at x=1014 against the 1016 limit (2px margin). The tagline is about 14px tall and illegible on a phone.
The lower third of the safe area (y~1380-1580) is unused in S2 and S3, so the content sits high.
The end card (13.5-17.5) does not restate the NO MOBILE / NO CAPCUT filter. This is acceptable by the brief, but a paused viewer gets no filter.
Film grain was dropped, so the frame is flatter than the poster.
best_ideas: The playhead stops on each clip and stamps it individually with the X badge, the hatch and an orange 'NO'. This is the most unmissable way to deliver the NO MOBILE / NO CAPCUT filter, and both clips are already legible as plain clips before the stamp.
'Professional desktop editors only' is set at 64px as its own white line with a check. It is the biggest, clearest version of the positive filter.
There is no dead air: each whip lands new readable copy within about 0.2 s (rules readable at 3.22, BENEFITS at 7.22, headline at 13.22). The whole message is delivered by 8.84 s.
A persistent HUD (WE'RE HIRING top-left, logo top-right, as on the poster) means every single frame says who is hiring, even if a viewer taps back in mid-story.
The benefit rows copy the poster (icon tiles, 60px titles, 42px subtitles, right-hand 88px numerals) and snap in on 0.5 s beats.
The CTA slides in at 13.5, so it is visible for about 3.75 s and pixel-still for 3.14 s. The total of 17.5 s is the shorter of the two.

defects: 0.00: the ghost-outline headline is faint (34% white and 55% orange strokes). At thumbnail size 'VIDEO EDITOR' reads, but the ghost 'WE'RE HIRING' is illegible until the wipe passes it at about 0.35 s.

3.45-4.40: about 1 s with no readable copy right after the hook. There is tilt blur from 3.45 to 3.75, empty navy and blank tracks from 3.70 to 3.85, then plain blue clips with no text drawing from 3.83 to 4.37. This is the highest tap-through risk in either build.
4.40-5.10: both NO clips and the check line are revealed letter by letter in a single 0.7 s sweep, with X badges 0.15 s apart. This is less emphatic than separate stamps.
'Professional desktop editors only' is only 42px inside a clip, so the positive filter is the smallest key message.
7.60-8.30: the second tilt is the same move, again with about 0.7 s of blurred or empty tracks before the BENEFITS header builds.

8.33-9.49: benefit clips slide in from the right and overflow past the right frame edge (x>1016) while moving. Titles at 52px and subtitles at 38px are smaller than kinetic's. 'PREMIUM STOCK & MOCKUP SUBSCRIPTION' wraps, and the numerals move to the left, unlike the poster.
S2 and S3 drop 'WE'RE HIRING' entirely (only the logo stays), so a mid-story frame does not say it is a hiring post.
9.49-14.07: 4.5 s of fully static benefits, the longest no-new-information hold of either build.
14.20-14.60: the double slash band travels about 3000px in 0.8 s, so frame-to-frame jumps are large. It covers the KRS logo at 14.33-14.40.
The CTA is only fully visible from about 14.6 (0.85 s later than kinetic). 'DM us your portfolio' is 37px and tight in the right half of the bar. At 17.9 s the video is at the 18 s cap.

The logo is centred at the top, the kicker sits above the headline and the streaks are in the corners, so the layout departs from the approved poster's kicker-left / logo-right top row. Film grain was dropped.
The playhead head parked at x≈1012 overlaps the top-right bracket corner in S1/S2 (decoration only).
best_ideas: At frame 0 the headline is a ghost outline, and the orange playhead 'renders' it solid with a clip-path wipe synced to it (0.12-1.02). Judged from my own renders under /home/user/kawin/posters/video-editor-hiring/story/judge-social/: frames extracted from both MP4s, side-by-side pairs with the Instagram UI zones tinted, 1/30 s frame strips around every transition, a thumbnail-size comparison, measured text extents and font sizes, and a frame-diff stillness timeline. Both MP4s meet the format spec: H.264 High, 1080x1920, yuv420p, 30 fps, 17.5 s and 17.9 s. Both use only the canonical copy, keep all text inside the safe area, and end on a still card with the logo, WE'RE HIRING, VIDEO EDITOR and APPLY NOW / DM us your portfolio. The end cards are nearly identical, so the decision comes down to how fast and how clearly each one delivers the message.

My lens is social and recruitment. Cinematic has the better first frame and the more sophisticated motion. Its ghost-outline 'VIDEO EDITOR' that the playhead renders solid by 0.95 s is the strongest idea in either build. But it spends about 1 s after the hook (3.45-4.40) on blur, empty navy and blank clips with no readable copy, and another 0.7 s after the second tilt (7.6-8.3). On Stories those are exactly the moments people tap away. It also delivers the NO MOBILE / NO CAPCUT filter in one quick 0.7 s sweep, with the positive line at only 42px, and it drops WE'RE HIRING from the middle scenes.

Kinetic hooks harder in motion: VIDEO slams in at 0.27-0.44 s and EDITOR is revealed by 1.06 s. Its frame 0 is weaker, with an empty centre. After that it never leaves the screen without readable copy: the rules are legible at 3.22, each NO clip is stamped one at a time, and the positive line is 64px. Its benefit rows copy the poster with larger type (60px titles, 42px subtitles), the whole message is delivered by 8.84 s, the CTA is visible for about 3.75 s, and it is 0.4 s shorter. Its weaknesses are repetitive identical whips, a long static benefits hold, and thin reading margins.

Winner: kinetic, 41 against 40. The recommended graft is cinematic's ghost-outline frame 0 with the playhead render wipe, plus the WE'RE HIRING kicker in the headline lockup, to fix kinetic's empty thumbnail. Swapping one of kinetic's three identical whips for cinematic's tilt (without its blank-track gap) would also help, as would adding cinematic's logo-slash glint on the end card.
